text: Cycles can be ridden on the ground or by pedal-powered means, such as bicycles or tricycles. In such cases, brakes are placed at the rear of the front wheel, and the tires are positioned in the front wheel. Tires are typically made of rubber and have a small amount of air to inflate when the rider goes down. Brakes are usually made of iron and have a small area on the rim called the brake pad. This brake pad fits into the hub, which is the wheel at the rear of the bike. As the rider pedals, the brake pad moves up and down, causing the brake to make contact with the tire. The brake system is usually controlled by a controller on the handlebar, which is attached to the rear of the bike. This controller is typically a combination of two pedals, one on each side of the bike.
